dlg.rook.valley.0.note: No warmth to spare. 'Ashford was.' on its own. The 'pet' is habit, not softness. The don'ts flat, each one a door closing, with no build.
dlg.rook.valley.0.beats: Ashford was. [beat] Half of it went to the Morrow in one night, pet, and the other half the year after, coughing. [breath] Don't ask Holloway about it. Don't ask Maeca. Don't ask a Kerchief, if you meet one. [beat] And don't ask me twice.

dlg.maeca.blind_ask.1.note: The narrator never shows a feeling. 'That's all.' plain; the weight is the fact.

dlg.wenna.mask.1.hides: what the fever year cost her
dlg.wenna.mask.1.note: A herbwife's practical pride in the bitterroot. 'Take it.' an order. 'I'm too old to go where it's needed.' plain, no self-pity.
dlg.wenna.mask.1.beats: My blightward. I made it the fever year. Stuff the beak with bitterroot and you can walk through air that'd drop a horse. [beat] Take it. I'm too old to go where it's needed.

dlg.wenna.tallow.0.note: Somerset bluntness. 'Fat was a pig.' as plain fact, a dry relish.
dlg.wenna.tallow.0.beats: I burn fat, child. [beat] Fat's honest. Fat was a pig.

dlg.chid.woke.2.hides: he carries you in himself, and what the flame costs
dlg.chid.woke.2.note: The lie wears thin: brighter than he feels. The joke about the carter, then the narrator: he laughs, and stops. The rest practical.
dlg.chid.woke.2.beats: You're awake! A carter found you. The same carter, as it happens; he's starting to think you're doing it on purpose. [laugh] | You'll be sore a day or two. Whatever did this is still out there. It'll have your things.

dlg.chid.woke.3.note: Tumbling relief; a catch on 'The flame kept you.' 'I watched it.' quiet wonder. Then practical.
dlg.chid.woke.3.beats: You're awake! Good. Good! A carter found you on the Old Road and brought you here, and the flame... [beat] The flame kept you. I watched it. [breath] You'll be sore a day or two. Whatever did this to you is still out there. It'll have your things. They always keep something.

dlg.chid.woke.4.note: 'Oh, you're awake.' soft surprise. The prayer told shyly; 'well.' a little shrug. 'Here you are.' warm.
dlg.chid.woke.4.beats: Oh, you're awake. A carter found you on the Old Road and brought you in, and I didn't know what else to do, so I prayed at the shrine and... [beat] well. Here you are. You'll be sore a day or two. Whatever did this is still out there. It'll have your things.

dlg.chid.carter.0.intent: the carter who keeps finding you
dlg.chid.carter.0.hides: there is no carter, or none he can name
dlg.chid.carter.0.note: Musing, light; he doesn't hear what he's saying. Narrator: the cup. Then fussing kindness; 'There's nothing in it but hot.' a small reassurance.
dlg.chid.carter.0.beats: ...You know, I never asked his name. [beat] I should ask his name. Next time. | Drink that. It's only hot water. [beat] There's nothing in it but hot.

bark.rook.said.0.note: Said to nobody; 'He's sent it back.' flat, a little hurt.

bark.rook.said.1.note: 'I know. Leave it.' stops the subject dead.

bark.holloway.said.0.note: A notice read aloud by a man who wrote it.

bark.holloway.said.2.note: To himself. 'That's one debt paid.' flat.

bark.maeca.said.6.note: The second 'Nothing.' quieter. No tears in it.

bark.chid.said.0.note: Cheerful and practical, like a broken pump.

bark.chid.said.2.note: 'Up's very good.' a little joke at himself.

bark.rav.said.0.note: Two words escaping him; barely voiced.

bark.harlan.said.0.note: Trying to sound unworried and failing.

bark.harlan.said.5.note: Fond memory with the fear under it.

bark.harlan.said.6.note: 'I keep going to look.' a happy confession.

bark.harlan.said.7.note: 'So do I, now.' a small admission.

bark.harlan.said.8.intent: the sign that won't be made
bark.harlan.said.8.note: He breaks off on the second 'Coyle and'; the cut is the line.

bark.tam.said.3.note: Upset, not sure he's allowed to be.

bark.tam.said.4.note: 'We've got no pipes.' the point he's sure of.

bark.brannoc.said.0.note: Few words; the hope hidden in the counting.

bark.keegan.said.0.note: Muttering 'Chapter four' twice, then a startled, proper 'Good morning.'

folk.109.note: A real question to a neighbour.

say.8c74ea2b0476.note: The rules plainly; 'from nothing.' level. A pause before the mother's face, and that sentence no softer than the rest.
say.8c74ea2b0476.beats: As the sun clears the trees, the ember goes out of you and back into the ground, and everything it gave you goes with it. What you carry, and what you have learned, are still yours. When the dark comes again, it will burn again, from nothing. [beat] You try to call up your mother's face, and find it is not quite where you left it.

say.2d8b284f0b0e.note: A pause before 'None go down to it.'
say.2d8b284f0b0e.beats: Prints in the frost, your own. They come up from the river. [beat] None go down to it.

cbark.db6c2c28509f.note: Drawn out, from under the water.

cbark.d6a6b3a4b868.note: Cut off mid-word, a sniff, then smug: delighted, never beaten.
cbark.d6a6b3a4b868.beats: Finders keepers, surface-m— [sniff] ...Downstairs'll be ever so grateful.

say.f45eec417fcc.note: Plain; the ordinary details do it.

say.2133e8a51219.note: Plain; no comment in the voice.

say.546ec60933f6.note: Three strokes, each its own beat; 'and steps back, and back.' level.
say.546ec60933f6.beats: ...Brannoc kneels at its head with an iron marker and his hammer: three strokes, [beat] iron into earth. [beat] Rook sets the inn's lamp at its foot, lit, in broad daylight, and steps back, [beat] and back.
